collapses_to.tool: a batch form of the same keyed upsert — many findings for one source in a single request, plus the set of externalIds that should now be resolved — so a repository with fifty findings is one call rather than fifty. Nothing about idempotency would change: the key is already documented and already server-side, so this is a throughput and rate-limit question rather than a correctness one

idempotency.verified_at: The "Idempotency/Upsert Behavior" section of https://api.noru.tech/llms.txt states that for `POST /v1/security-findings`, if `source + externalId` already exists in the organization the request returns 200 and updates the existing finding, and otherwise returns 201 and creates one. The endpoint's own "Behavior" note repeats it and documents `externalId` as "Source-native unique ID. Create is idempotent per (source, externalId)". The createSecurityFinding tool description published by https://api.noru.tech/v1/mcp says the same thing and adds that it uses the write:risks scope, matching REST.

source.note: Every finding this piece already has open in the organization. This is the half of the queue a repository cannot know: a rule that stopped firing has left a finding open somewhere, and a scan that only ever adds is a scan whose register grows for ever.
The organization's own asset inventory, so a finding attaches to an asset the register already holds, by that register's external id. This plugin ships no asset list and never creates one.
The organization's own risk register, so a finding can be filed against a risk it already carries. This plugin never opens a risk.
